subject: SLA usage-bucketing & ops retainer — proposal and ask
messages:
From: Aisha Rahman <aisha.rahman@redwood.com>

Cc: Sara Mitchell <s.mitchell@brightline.ai>
Date: 2027-05-09T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: SLA proposal — compact retainer modules (initial)
Attachments: SLA_Retainer_Options_v3.pdf

Hi Ben / Sara,

Thanks again for the call this morning — good to hear more about how Brightline plans to scale inference across peak campaign windows. I promised a concise set of options for the SLA/ops retainer we discussed. Attached is a short deck (SLA_Retainer_Options_v3.pdf) that lays out a compact approach:

- Core SLA (uptime bands + token-based baseline)
- Rapid Escalation Retainer (dedicated on-call hours + guaranteed 2-hour response for Sev1)
- Usage Buckets (pre-purchased throughput credits for burst traffic)

Key asks from you: which of the above you want priced as a) a standard month-to-month add-on vs b) a committed 12-month retainer (we can provide a stepped discount for commitment).

Two clarifications I want to call out up front:
1) Usage buckets are additive to the baseline token consumption — they activate only when traffic exceeds the baseline allotment. They don't change latency SLOs but can be assigned to overflow capacity to avoid throttling.
2) Short pilots: we can offer up to $5k in pilot credits against the retainer if you sign a 3-month pilot within 30 days.

If that sounds right, I can send a short priced proposal with two options (standard vs committed) by EOD. Want to schedule 30 minutes tomorrow to run through numbers?

Best,
Aisha
Aisha Rahman
Director, Solutions & Strategic GTM
Redwood Inference

Aisha, thanks for the summary and attachment — useful. A few quick questions from our side before you send pricing:

1) How do the usage buckets interact with latency SLOs? If we route overflow to buckets, will Redwood guarantee the same 99.9% p95 latency, or is overflow best-effort?
2) Can you provide sample pricing for a 3-tier usage bucket (monthly 0-5M tokens baseline, 5-20M burst, 20M+ overflow) under both month-to-month and 12-month commit?
3) Procurement asks: do you have a standard termination clause for material SLA breaches? We may need a 30-day cure/termination window.

Also — can you confirm whether pilot credits can be applied against month one invoice if we convert to a retainer after pilot? Procurement flagged that as a requirement.

If you can send a short priced options doc and a proposed minimal SOW (or link to your standard SOW), we can get internal finance/procurement eyes on it.

Thanks,
Ben
VP Ops, Brightline AI

Aisha — draft below, keeping it tight. Numbers are ballpark (we should round at quote time). I attached the worksheet with the math.

Option A — Standard (month-to-month)
- Core SLA: $5,000/mo (baseline platform + monitoring) — includes 0-5M tokens
- Usage bucket: $0.0035 per additional token up to 20M; $0.0028 per token beyond 20M
- Rapid Escalation Retainer: $2,500/mo (up to 8 on-call hours, 4-hour Sev1 response window)

Option B — Committed 12mo retainer (prepay quarterly)
- Core SLA: $4,400/mo (12% discount)
- Usage bucket: $0.0029 per additional token up to 20M; $0.0024 per token beyond 20M
- Rapid Escalation Retainer: $2,000/mo (12% discount)
- Additional concession: pilot credit of $5,000 applied to first invoice when conversion occurs within 30 days

Recommended policy on latency SLOs and buckets:
- Baseline tokens served from committed capacity with full latency SLO (99.9% p95).
- Usage buckets are backed by overflow capacity that we route based on cost/latency policy. For committed retainer customers we can guarantee p95 latency for the first overflow bucket band (5-20M); beyond that (overflow beyond pre-purchased capacity) we treat as best-effort with a documented target (target p95 120ms but not SLA-backed).

On the procurement request (30-day termination for material SLA breach): standard Redwood SOW includes a 60-day cure period for major infra breaches; legal can make an exception to 30 days for an exec-approved enterprise commit (would need approval from revenue leadership).

If Brightline wants the additional 5% discount beyond the committed pricing, we need an exec exception and a small increase in volume commitment or a multi-year clause. Otherwise suggest we hold at 12-18% range.

Happy to sync and finalize language.

— Jonas
Head of Pricing Operations, Redwood Inference

Ben / Sara / Procurement,

Thanks for the fast follow. Per our internal convo, attaching two priced options and the worksheet: the short version below.

Option A — Standard (month-to-month)
- Core SLA: $5,000/mo — includes baseline 0–5M tokens
- Usage buckets: $0.0035/token (5–20M), $0.0028/token (20M+)

Option B — Committed 12-mo retainer
